national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today emphasised that self-reliance in defence sector can be achieved through seamless collaboration among the Defence Forces, Research and Development institutions and the industry. He called for greater dialogue, co-development and co-production to accelerate technology adoption and strengthen India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem. Addressing the DRDO-Industry Synergy Meet, ‘VIMARSH 2026’ in New Delhi, Mr Singh said that DRDO has demonstrated its capabilities in every field, from missiles to radars, combat aircraft to submarines, electronic warfare system to Artificial Intelligence. The Defence Minister said that the reforms witnessed in the defence sector over the past few years are unprecedented and several game-changing decisions have also been taken. These include the Positive Indigenisation List, the Make in India initiative, iDEX, ADITI and the decision to allocate 25 percent of the Defence Research and Development budget to the private sector. Mr Singh asserted that these measures have been taken to ensure that India does not remain dependent on imports in the defence sector, but moves towards self-reliance. Describing MSMEs as a backbone of the Indian economy, Mr Singh said that their contribution in components, sub-systems and essential services is significant in the defence sector. He added that MSMEs will have to continuously focus on quality, delivery, innovation and global standards, as well as increase partnerships with large companies. The Defence Minister stressed that a new wave of defence startups is rising in India. He said that these startups are not only innovative but also agile and are disrupting the traditional defence manufacturing model. The Minister said that the opportunities in the defence sector have increased for them with funding, mentorship, and market access.

national_raw_news.title: 36 mins ago | National 217 India committed to promoting circular economy as part of sustainable development, says Environmen...
national_raw_news.content: Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav underlined India’s commitment to embedding circular economy principles into its sustainable development framework. The Minister stressed that India has modernized it’s deep rooted ancient cultural practices of reuse, repair, and conservation values into contemporary policies under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Addressing the inaugural session of the 10th edition of World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026, at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar today, the Minister emphasised initiatives such as Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations and Mission life as crucial steps in its circularity journey. Highlighting global collaborations like the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, India-EU joint framework, and Mission LiFE, the Minister stated that circularity must begin at home. Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel inaugurated the forum which is being held for the first time in India. Addressing the Forum, the Chief Minister stressed that growth, ecology, prosperity, and sustainability must go hand in hand, framing circular economy principles as the core of India’s sustainable trajectory. Over 2,000 stakeholders from more than 65 countries are taking part in the forum which is being held under the theme ‘Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity,’. As of August 2026, over 83,000 producers and 4,802 recyclers are registered under EPR, processing nearly 482.24 lakh metric tonnes of waste. The global event is jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Central Pollution Control Board, Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, and the Government of Gujarat. Over the two days, the forum will host 4 plenary sessions and 16 thematic sessions covering key areas such as the application of AI, green energy, sustainable finance, governance, and the start-up ecosystem. This will be followed by 80 accelerator sessions hosted globally on September 17th and 18th. Additionally, an international expo featuring over 125 exhibitors will showcase innovative, practical solutions for circular business models. Speaking at the inaugural session, Ambassador of Finland to India, Mikko Kivikoski, said that circular economy is not just an environmental agenda which is limited to West management. He stressed that emerging economies like India has a pivotal role in strengthening the circular economy framework.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 96 National Engineers’ Day marks birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna M Visvesvaraya
national_raw_news.content: National Engineers’ Day is being celebrated today to honor the birth anniversary of Bharat Ratna Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya, one of India’s greatest engineers. The day is celebrated every year on 15th September to remember Visvesvaraya’s contributions and honour the role of engineers in the nation’s growth. Vice-President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tributes to M Visvesvaraya on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, the Vice-President said that M Visvesvaraya was a legendary engineer and visionary nation-builder whose contributions continue to inspire generations. Mr Radhakrishnan said that engineers drive India’s progress through innovation, technology and transformative solutions that advance the lives of people and the nation. He wished that the country’s engineers continue to innovate and build a stronger, more prosperous Viksit Bharat. Mr Modi said that M. Visvesvaraya was an engineering genius whose nation-building vision continues to inspire citizens. The Prime Minister extended his greetings to engineers for their contributions to building, innovating, and providing solutions for a better tomorrow. In a social media post, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that M Visvesvaraya’s life remains an enduring example of excellence, discipline, innovation and public service. Mr Singh added that his extraordinary contribution to India’s nation-building journey will always be remembered. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that M Visvesvaraya’s remarkable contributions played a crucial role in nation-building. Extending greetings to engineers, the Home Minister said that their relentless innovations drive India’s progress through perpetual growth.
